nodes.name: FeOOH nanorods arrays on CFC substrate
Hydrothermal FeOOH synthesis
nodes.procedure: FeOOH nanorods arrays on CFC substrate was synthesized by a typical hydrothermal method at 120°C for 6 h. Commercial carbon cloth was chosen as a binder-free substrate for catalyst growth.
nodes.source_text: First, FeOOH nanorods arrays on CFC substrate was synthesized by a typical hydrothermal method at 120°C for 6 h.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal sulfurization to FeMo-S
nodes.procedure: FeMo-S nanosheets were obtained through a second hydrothermal sulfurization treatment of FeOOH precursors in sodium molybdate and thiourea solution via anion exchange reaction. The nanorod-like morphology of FeOOH was disrupted under high-temperature hydrothermal conditions at 200°C for 24 h, resulting in the uniform and interconnected distribution of smooth nanosheets on the entire CFC substrate.

nodes.description: SOR performance evaluation in varying Na2S concentrations, optimal at 1M NaOH + 2.43M Na2S

current_density_at_0.5_V_vs_RHE.value: nearly five times higher than Pt/C

nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic efficacy of FeMo-S/Ru for SOR was initially evaluated in a 1M NaOH solution with varying concentrations of Na2S, ranging from 0 to 2.43M. As depicted in Figure 4a, FeMo-S/Ru clearly demonstrates the most superior SOR performance when measured in a solution of 1M NaOH + 2.43M Na2S... It notably achieves current densities of 100 and 300mA cm-2 at low potentials of 0.30 and 0.54V versus RHE, respectively... FeMo-S/Ru shows a Tafel slope of 14.7mVdec-1... FeMo-S/Ru delivers an outstanding long-term stability with negligible decay at the current density of 10mAcm-2.

The HER catalytic performance of FeMo-S/Ru was also tested in 1M NaOH electrolyte. The LSV curves in Figure 4g demonstrate that FeMo-S/Ru achieves a current density of 10mAcm-2 with a small overpotential of 85.9mV... FeMo-S/Ru displays significantly lower overpotentials of 244.9 and 315.1mV at the substantial current densities of 200 and 350mA cm-2, respectively... FeMo-S/Ru possesses a small Tafel slope of 43.0mVdec-1... the overpotential experienced only slight changes during 90h of continuous electrolysis at a current density of 10mAcm-2.

nodes.description: Two-electrode SOR/HER coupling system for sulfion degradation-assisted H2 production
nodes.source_text: a two-electrode electrocatalytic coupling system was constructed, utilizing FeMo-S/Ru as both the anode and cathode catalysts... The SOR/HER cell achieves... current densities of 100 and 200mA cm-2 at voltages of 0.57 and 0.69V, respectively... the long-term galvanostatic test at a current density of 100mA cm-2 demonstrated that the voltage... could be effectively maintained at ≈0.57V for continuous operation over 838h or 34 days... a stable rate of hydrogen generation at ≈0.735 mL min-1 demonstrated a Faraday efficiency of over 96%.

nodes.source_text: The electrochemical surface areas (ECSA) were initially evaluated by measuring the electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) through CV curves in the non-faradaic region... The Cdl values of FeMoS/Ru, FeMo-S, FeSx, and MoS2 catalysts are 725.9, 357.3, 14.3, and 126.3mFcm-2, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Characteristic diffraction peaks of FeMo-S/Ru consistent with FeMo-S at 14.9°, 17.1°, 24.6°, 31.3°, 34.5°, 44.6°, and 57.2° corresponding to monoclinic FeMo2S4 phase; absence of Ru peaks verifies high dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S2a (Supporting Information), FeMo-S sample exhibited characteristic diffraction peaks at 14.9°, 17.1°, 24.6°, 31.3°, 34.5°, 44.6°, and 57.2° corresponding to the (002), (202), (113), (022), (221), (115), and (227) lattice planes of monoclinic FeMo2S4 phase ... The characteristic diffraction peaks of FeMo-S/Ru are consistent with FeMo-S.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show FeMo-S/Ru retains nanosheet architecture with roughened surface and numerous nanoparticles anchored.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images collectively demonstrate that the nanosheet architecture is well preserved, while also exhibiting a roughened surface with numerous nanoparticles anchored on it (Figure 2a-c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ultrafine Ru nanoparticles uniformly dispersed on FeMo-S nanosheets with average size 3.2 nm; lattice spacings of 5.93 Å (FeMo2S4 (002)), 2.86 Å (FeMo2S4 (022)), and 2.14 Å (Ru (002)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2e, ultrafine Ru nanoparticles are uniformly dispersed on the FeMo-S nanosheets without evident aggregation. The size-distribution histograms (Figure 2f) confirm an average size of 3.2 nm. Furthermore, the interplanar spacings obtained from the lattice stripes ... confirm the phase spacings of 2.86 and 2.14 Å corresponding to the (022) phase of FeMo2S4 and the (002) phase of Ru, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ultrafine Ru nanoparticles uniformly dispersed; cross-section shows ultrathin FeMo-S nanosheets with 5.93 Å (002) spacing; elemental mapping confirms uniform Fe, Mo, S, Ru distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image (Figure 2d) reveals the cross-section of the ultrathin nanosheets ... It exhibits a distinct lattice spacing of 5.93 Å corresponding to the (002) plane of FeMo2S4 ... HAADF-STEM image, and the corresponding element mappings revealed that the FeMo-S/Ru heterostructure consists of evenly distributed Fe, Mo, S, and Ru elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows concentric diffraction rings matching multiphases of FeMo2S4 and Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2h displays a corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern, revealing multiple concentric diffraction rings that closely match the multiphases of FeMo2S4 and Ru.
the energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectrum reveals an atomic ratio of 1:2.01:0.06 for Fe, Mo, and Ru, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru content in FeMo-S/Ru is 0.8 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru content in FeMo-S/Ru heterostructure was further estimated to be 0.8 wt% by inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometer (ICP-AES).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeMo-S/Ru shows Fe2+ (707.5/720.3 eV, 86% Fe3+), Mo4+/Mo6+ (228.5/231.7, 232.7/235.3 eV), S2-/S22- (161.4/162.6/164.0 eV), Ru0 (462.1/484.5 eV) and Ru4+ (464.5/486.8 eV); negative shifts indicate electron redistribution at heterointerfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution Fe 2p spectra of FeMo-S/Ru (Figure 3c), the deconvoluted peaks at 707.5 and 720.3 eV are assigned to the 2p3/2 and 2p1/2 of the Fe2+ species ... The XPS results unveil the robust interface interaction between Ru nanoclusters and FeMo-S nanosheets, leading to electron redistribution at the heterointerfaces.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical double-layer capacitance Cdl of FeMo-S/Ru is 725.9 mF/cm² on CFC and 46.8 mF/cm² on carbon paper, indicating more accessible electroactive sites than FeMo-S (357.3/42.7 mF/cm²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl values of FeMoS/Ru, FeMo-S, FeSx, and MoS2 catalysts are 725.9, 357.3, 14.3, and 126.3 mFcm⁻², respectively ... the Cdl values of FeMo-S/Ru, FeMo-S, FeSx, MoS2, and CP are 46.8, 42.7, 5.1, 36.8, and 2.3 mFcm⁻², respectively.
